beats.text: Japan judges an affair more mildly than its neighbors.
In a 2025 survey, sixty-five percent of Japanese called an affair wrong. The taller the block, the higher that share.
In South Korea, it was eighty-three. In the US, ninety.
At home, nearly half of married people in Japan had no sex in the past month.
What marriage means, and what it allows, really depends on the country.

sources: Pew Research Center (5 March 2026), 25-country survey on morality, fielded Jan–May 2025: 'married people having an affair' morally unacceptable – Japan 65 %, South Korea 83 %, US 90 % (morally wrong).

Japan Family Planning Association (JFPA), survey on the lifestyles and attitudes of men and women, conducted Sept–Oct 2023: 3,000 randomly selected people aged 16–49, response rate 26.6 %; 'nearly half' of married respondents sexless (no intercourse for a month or more), via Japan Times 18 March 2024. Earlier JFPA wave 2016: 47.2 % of married respondents (nippon.com). A commercial online survey (Jex Japan Sex Survey 2024) reports 64.2 %.
